policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the pair asyndetically, 'to be in subjection to rulers, to authorities', with no conjunction joining them; the RP reading's added kai would surface as 'rulers and authorities' (so KJV, 'principalities and powers'). The ASV's departure from that wording distinguishes the base text.

The variant is only the case of the relative pronoun (accusative ha vs. genitive by attraction hon) with no difference in sense; ASV 'works done in righteousness, which we did ourselves' renders either identically. Both verse notes are classed alternative_rendering (laver; and through renewing) and touch other words, so nothing maps to this unit.

Neuter to eleos and masculine ton eleon are declensional forms of the same noun with the same meaning; ASV 'according to his mercy' is produced by either. The two notes here are alternative_rendering and concern 'washing' and 'renewing', so neither maps to this unit.

Aorist passive-form genethomen and middle genometha are alternative subjunctives of ginomai with the same sense 'become'; ASV 'we might be made heirs' matches either, as KJV's identical 'should be made heirs' on the RP reading shows. The single note is alternative_rendering about the placement of 'according to hope'.

The RP addition is the article ta before the predicate adjectives; ASV 'These things are good and profitable unto men' is the natural rendering with or without it, KJV giving the same English from the articled text. The note is alternative_rendering about 'maintain good works'.

ASV has the plural 'strifes' alongside 'questionings' and 'fightings'; the WH reading eris is singular accusative, which would give 'strife'. The number of the English noun distinguishes plural ereis.
Apollon and Apollo are competing accusative spellings of the same personal name; ASV 'Apollos' reflects the nominative form of the name and cannot distinguish the accusative ending.
ASV ends the epistle 'Grace be with you all.' with no closing 'Amen', so the RP addition of Amen is not represented in the English.
